identity.title: Pan-LUT: Efficient Pan-sharpening via Learnable Look-Up Tables

problem.claim: Enable efficient pan-sharpening of large remote-sensing images while balancing performance and computational cost.

gap.claim: Existing deep-learning pan-sharpening methods impose substantial inference overhead, limiting use in real-world settings without dedicated accelerators.

contributions.claim: Pan-LUT, a learnable LUT framework with PAN-guided spectral mapping, spatial-detail modeling, and adaptive output aggregation.
A lightweight model reported to contain fewer than 700K parameters and support very large-image processing.
Extension of the method to general image-fusion tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present Pan-LUT as a novel learnable LUT framework for efficient pan-sharpening.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report processing 15K×15K remote-sensing images on a 24GB GPU.
The authors report processing a 9K×9K image in under 1 ms on one RTX 2080 Ti GPU, with significantly faster performance than other methods.
The authors report that Pan-LUT surpasses SOTA methods on full-resolution scenes under real-world conditions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep-learning pan-sharpening improves on traditional methods but carries high inference cost, especially for large images and hardware-constrained deployment.
The authors propose Pan-LUT to balance image-processing performance and computational efficiency.
PGLUT handles channel-wise spectral mapping, SDLUT captures fine spatial details, and AOLUT adaptively aggregates channel information.
The authors report lightweight large-image processing, faster runtime than other methods, and higher performance than SOTA methods in stated full-resolution real-world scenes.
The method is also extended to general image-fusion tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract ties each named LUT component to a distinct image-fusion function: spectral mapping, spatial-detail capture, or output aggregation.

lessons.interpretation: Mapping modules to explicit failure-relevant functions makes the method's design rationale easier to evaluate.
lessons.application: For a multi-stage vision method, state each component's targeted signal or bottleneck alongside its role.
lessons.exception: This framing is less useful when modules are intentionally generic or their roles cannot be separated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, quantitative quality metrics, baselines, or the exact hardware and measurement protocol for the comparisons.
The scope and evidence for the general image-fusion extension are not described.
The reported runtime and image-size claims do not establish reproducibility or independently verified effectiveness.
